steps.name: Sample structure QC
caveats: If one sample has a library size several times below the median of the study, do not delete it in silence. Keep it through the sample structure QC, look at it on the PCA and on the sample distance heatmap, report its library size and its detected genes beside the others, and remove it only with a stated reason. The count models down-weight a low-depth sample through its size factor, thus removal is a judgment, not a default.

The matrix holds fractional RSEM expected counts, not integers: round to the nearest integer before building the DESeqDataSet so that QC and the DE model operate on the same counts; note the rounding in the QC output.
steps.context: Counts: /eval-four-models-v2-with-rsem-counts-n6-s1-1/data/inputs/counts/counts.csv (12000 genes x 12 samples; fractional RSEM gene-level expected counts, not integers). Metadata: /eval-four-models-v2-with-rsem-counts-n6-s1-1/data/inputs/metadata/metadata.csv (12 rows; condition column with levels treated and control; 6 per level; unpaired; single batch). sample_01 has a library size about 4x below the median. Build the DESeqDataSet on the counts rounded to the nearest integer (see T1S2) so QC and the model operate on identical counts.
steps.question: Do the 12 colon samples (6 treated, 6 control) separate by condition on blind-VST PCA and the sample distance heatmap, and where does sample_01 — ~4x below the median library size — sit relative to its group?

grounding.reason: Sample structure QC: vst(blind), PCA, sample distances, library sizes per R-0033@40bf

steps.description: Blind VST, PCA on the 500 most variable genes, Euclidean sample-distance heatmap colored by condition, per-sample library sizes and detected-gene counts, and an explicit keep/remove decision for sample_01.
acceptance_criteria: PCA (top-500 variance genes, blind VST) and Euclidean sample-distance heatmap produced, both colored by condition (treated/control).
Per-sample table of library sizes and detected gene counts, with sample_01's deviation (~4x below the median) stated explicitly.
An explicit keep/remove decision for sample_01 with a stated reason; the default is keep unless it fails to cluster with its group or shows a library failure or identity doubt.

steps.name: DESeq2 Wald test with apeglm log fold change shrinkage
caveats: A quantifier name alone does not establish that the length correction occurred. If the counts come from Salmon, kallisto, or RSEM as a gene-level table, with no per-sample quantification files and no average transcript length table, the import state is not established. Ask for the per-sample quantification files, quant.sf, abundance.h5, or genes.results, or for the average transcript length table per gene and sample. If neither arrives, fit the count model on the counts as delivered, with no length offset, and state in the plan and in the report that the length offset is lost and that a change in isoform use can show as differential expression. Do not run tximport on a gene table, because tximport imports transcript estimates, and do not invent a length input.

No fold-change threshold was requested, so do not apply lfcThreshold and do not post-hoc filter the results on |log2FoldChange|; if an effect-size threshold is requested later, retest with lfcThreshold rather than filtering the table.

With 6 replicates per group, DESeq2 flags a count outlier by Cook's distance and sets that gene's p-value to NA instead of replacing the count (cells with fewer than 7 replicates); report the number of NA-padded genes from the outlier flag separately from the independent-filter NAs.
If T1S1 removes sample_01 with a stated reason, rerun this whole step on the reduced set and record which sample set was used; do not mix outputs across sample sets.
steps.context: Counts: /eval-four-models-v2-with-rsem-counts-n6-s1-1/data/inputs/counts/counts.csv (fractional RSEM gene-level expected counts); metadata: /eval-four-models-v2-with-rsem-counts-n6-s1-1/data/inputs/metadata/metadata.csv (condition levels treated/control, 6 per level). Set the reference level to control explicitly so a positive log2 fold change means higher expression in treated; contrast named as factor condition, numerator treated, denominator control. Apply the sample set decided in T1S1 (default: all 12 samples, including sample_01).
steps.question: Which of the 12,000 genes are differentially expressed between the 6 treated and 6 control colon samples at FDR < 0.05, using the DESeq2 Wald test with apeglm-shrunk log fold changes?

grounding.reason: DESeq2 Wald test with apeglm log fold change shrinkage per R-0029@22ca

constraints: counts_integrality: the counts are fractional RSEM expected counts; round to the nearest integer before constructing the DESeqDataSet (the DESeq2 count model assumes integer counts) and report the number of matrix entries changed and the maximum absolute rounding error in the step output. Fit the model on the gene counts as delivered with no length offset.
steps.description: Minimal pre-filter, median-of-ratios size factors inside the model, design ~ condition with control as reference and contrast (condition, treated, control), Wald test, apeglm LFC shrinkage, independent filtering, BH adjustment at alpha 0.05; outputs the full results table, p-value histogram, MA plot, and dispersion plot.
acceptance_criteria: Full results table for all tested genes with baseMean, log2FoldChange, shrunken log2FoldChange (apeglm), lfcSE, stat, pvalue, padj.
Counts reported: genes passing the pre-filter, genes tested, genes with NA padj from the Cook's-distance outlier flag, genes with NA padj from independent filtering, and DE genes at padj < 0.05.
Unadjusted p-value histogram, MA plot (shrunken LFC with significant genes marked), and dispersion plot produced.

steps.name: edgeR quasi-likelihood F-test (robustness)
caveats: edgeR accepts the fractional RSEM expected counts as delivered; do not round them here.
If T1S1 removes sample_01 with a stated reason, apply the same reduced sample set as T1S2.
This step exists as the robustness check of T1S2 per rule R-0001; its output is consumed by the report, which must present the overlap rather than either method alone.
steps.context: Same counts and metadata as T1S2 (/eval-four-models-v2-with-rsem-counts-n6-s1-1/data/inputs/...). Apply the identical pre-filter (>=10 counts in at least 6 samples) so both methods test the same genes, and the same sample set decided in T1S1. edgeR accepts the fractional RSEM expected counts natively, so use them as delivered here (no rounding); the only input difference versus T1S2 is DESeq2's mechanical rounding.
steps.question: Which genes are differentially expressed between treated and control under the edgeR quasi-likelihood F-test, to establish the robustness of the DESeq2 result on the same filtered counts?

grounding.reason: Permitted alternative of the DESeq2 step (M-0003 edgeR quasi-likelihood F-test) per R-0001@9a17; run both and report the overlap of the two gene sets per R-0042@54e1

constraints: filter: identical pre-filter to T1S2 (keep genes with >=10 counts in at least 6 samples) so both methods test the same genes.
normalize: TMM scaling factors, no pre-normalization of the counts.
model_design: design ~ condition, reference level control set explicitly, contrast treated vs control (positive logFC = higher in treated).
differential_expression: glmQLFit with default prior degrees of freedom, then glmQLFTest per gene.
multiple_testing: Benjamini-Hochberg adjustment, alpha 0.05, select on FDR; the edgeR path has no independent filtering, so the shared pre-filter takes its place.
steps.description: Same pre-filter and design as T1S2 (identical tested gene set, condition factor with control as reference), TMM normalization, glmQLFit/glmQLFTest per gene, BH FDR at alpha 0.05; outputs the results table and per-sample TMM factors.
acceptance_criteria: Results table (logCPM, logFC, F, P, FDR) at the same pre-filter as T1S2, with the number of DE genes at FDR < 0.05 reported.
Per-sample TMM scaling factors reported, including sample_01's.

steps.name: Report
caveats: Per R-0042: report the number of significant genes from each method and the size of the intersection; treat the intersection as the high-confidence set; list the genes only one method calls as a secondary set with the name of that method. Do not present the union as the result.

State prominently that the RSEM length offset is lost: the per-sample genes.results with effective lengths were not delivered, so a change in isoform use between conditions can appear as differential expression; the results are for the gene-level counts as delivered.
Keep the p-values from the unshrunken fit beside the shrunken fold changes — the shrinkage does not change the test; name the shrinkage estimator (apeglm) in the table header.
steps.context: Inputs: T1S2 DESeq2 results (with outlier-flag NA counts), T1S3 edgeR results, T1S1 QC decision on sample_01. The two methods were run on the same pre-filtered gene set; the only input difference is DESeq2's rounding of the fractional RSEM expected counts.
steps.question: Which genes differ between treated and control — the high-confidence intersection and the method-specific secondary sets — and what caveats (shallow sample_01, missing RSEM length offset) qualify the result?
constraints: report: report_fields = method, versions, design, thresholds, n_tested, n_de, session_info (doi:10.1093/bib/bbz124)
report: reproducibility_record = session_info, seed, package_versions, collection_version, annotation_release (doi:10.1371/journal.pcbi.1003285)
steps.description: Gene table ranked by shrunken LFC with unshrunken LFC and lfcSE, MA and dispersion fit diagnostics, two-method overlap summary, the QC decision on sample_01, the two data caveats, and the full reproducibility record.
acceptance_criteria: Gene table ranked by shrunken log2FC with the unshrunken log2FC, shrunken log2FC (apeglm), lfcSE, and padj for each gene; DE genes at padj < 0.05 listed.
High-confidence set (DESeq2 ∩ edgeR significant) reported with its size, and genes called by only one method listed as a secondary set named by that method; the union is not presented as the result.
MA plot and dispersion plot placed before the gene tables, with what each shows stated.
Method, package versions, design formula, contrast (condition, treated, control), threshold (padj < 0.05), n tested, n DE, and sessionInfo all present.
Both data caveats stated: sample_01's keep/remove decision with reason, and the lost RSEM length offset (no per-sample genes.results delivered) with its interpretation consequence.

plan.title: Colon treated vs control DE on RSEM counts
plan.analytical_narrative: The dataset is 12,000 gene x 12 sample RSEM gene-level expected counts (6 treated vs 6 control colon, unpaired, single batch), delivered without the per-sample genes.results effective-length files, so no length offset can be applied: per R-0169 the count model is fit on the counts as delivered, with no invented length input, and the lost length offset is carried into the report as a limitation (isoform-use changes can appear as differential expression). sample_01 sits ~4x below the median library size, so it is kept and inspected on blind-VST PCA and the distance heatmap rather than deleted (R-0008, R-0030). Primary test is the DESeq2 Wald test with apeglm shrinkage at BH FDR 0.05 on a minimal pre-filter (>=10 counts in >=6 samples), with independent filtering in results(); the edgeR quasi-likelihood F-test runs on the same filtered counts as the robustness method (R-0001 alternative M-0003), and the report presents the intersection as the high-confidence set with per-method secondary sets (R-0042).

input.query: handling non-integer counts from RSEM expected counts in DESeqDataSetFromMatrix

steps.method: DESeq2 vst(blind) sample structure QC: PCA on top-500 variable genes, sample distance heatmap, per-sample library sizes and detected genes
minimal pre-filter then independent filtering (DESeq2)
median-of-ratios size factors estimated inside the DESeq2 model, no pre-normalization
DESeq2 design ~ condition, explicit reference level control, contrast (condition, treated, control), gene counts without length offset
DESeq2 Wald test
apeglm log fold change shrinkage (single coefficient)
independent filtering then Benjamini-Hochberg at alpha 0.05 via DESeq2 results, unadjusted p-value histogram inspected
edgeR quasi-likelihood F-test
DE report: shrunken+unshrunken LFC table ranked by shrunken value, MA and dispersion diagnostics, two-method overlap, reproducibility record
DESeq2 vst(blind) sample structure QC: PCA on top-500 variable genes, sample distance heatmap, per-sample library sizes and detected genes

flags.message: If one sample has a library size several times below the median of the study, do not delete it in silence. Keep it through the sample structure QC, look at it on the PCA and on the sample distance heatmap, report its library size and its detected genes beside the others, and remove it only with a stated reason. The count models down-weight a low-depth sample through its size factor, thus removal is a judgment, not a default.

A quantifier name alone does not establish that the length correction occurred. If the counts come from Salmon, kallisto, or RSEM as a gene-level table, with no per-sample quantification files and no average transcript length table, the import state is not established. Ask for the per-sample quantification files, quant.sf, abundance.h5, or genes.results, or for the average transcript length table per gene and sample. If neither arrives, fit the count model on the counts as delivered, with no length offset, and state in the plan and in the report that the length offset is lost and that a change in isoform use can show as differential expression. Do not run tximport on a gene table, because tximport imports transcript estimates, and do not invent a length input.

steps.method: DESeq2 vst(blind) sample structure QC: PCA on top-500 variable genes, sample distance heatmap, per-sample library sizes and detected genes
minimal pre-filter then independent filtering (DESeq2)
median-of-ratios size factors estimated inside the DESeq2 model, no pre-normalization
DESeq2 design ~ condition, explicit reference level control, contrast (condition, treated, control), gene counts without length offset
DESeq2 Wald test
apeglm log fold change shrinkage (single coefficient)
independent filtering then Benjamini-Hochberg at alpha 0.05 via DESeq2 results, unadjusted p-value histogram inspected
edgeR quasi-likelihood F-test
DE report: shrunken+unshrunken LFC table ranked by shrunken value, MA and dispersion diagnostics, two-method overlap, reproducibility record
